struct.name: PI_CPU_PROTECT
struct.from: public Linux SN0 Hub processor-interface header, Linux v4.0 (names, offsets, masks and shifts)
struct.doc: CPU protection register, named PI_CPU_PROTECT in the header. The header gives no fields. The IRIX register table confirms the access.

struct.name: PI_PROT_OVERRIDE
struct.from: public Linux SN0 Hub processor-interface header, Linux v4.0 (names, offsets, masks and shifts)
struct.doc: Protection override register, named PI_PROT_OVRRD in the header as the way to clear a CPU protection bit. The header gives neither an unlock value nor a behaviour, so none is imported. The IRIX register table confirms the access.

struct.name: PI_IO_PROTECT
struct.from: public Linux SN0 Hub processor-interface header, Linux v4.0 (names, offsets, masks and shifts)
struct.doc: Interrupt pending protection register, named PI_IO_PROTECT in the header. The header gives no fields. The IRIX register table confirms the access.

struct.name: PI_NMI_B
struct.from: public Linux SN0 Hub processor-interface header, Linux v4.0 (names, offsets, masks and shifts)
struct.doc: Non-maskable interrupt to processor B, named PI_NMI_B in the header and paired with the processor A register at the same stride. The IRIX register table confirms the access.

struct.name: PI_SOFTRESET
struct.from: public Linux SN0 Hub processor-interface header, Linux v4.0 (names, offsets, masks and shifts)
struct.doc: Soft reset, named PI_SOFTRESET in the header with the comment that it resets both processors. The header gives no value and no fields, so the data written is not imported. The IRIX register table confirms the access.

struct.name: PI_INT_PEND_MOD
struct.from: census: 9 sites, 8 routines (w); census: 8 sites, 8 routines (w, indexed)
struct.doc: Layout of the interrupt pending modify register, pi_int_pend_mod, as Linux writes it: a set bit and an interrupt level. Linux only writes the register. Whether a second processor in a node reaches it at another offset is not established by a public source and is not recorded.

struct.doc: Cross-call interrupt pending set for processor B, named PI_CC_PEND_SET_B in the header. The header's pairing rule puts it eight bytes above the processor A set. The IRIX register table confirms the access.

struct.name: PI_NACK_CNT_A
struct.from: public Linux SN0 Hub processor-interface header, Linux v4.0 (names, offsets, masks and shifts)
struct.doc: Consecutive negative-acknowledge counter for processor A, named PI_NACK_CNT_A in the header. The IRIX register table confirms the access.

struct.name: PI_NACK_CNT_B
struct.from: public Linux SN0 Hub processor-interface header, Linux v4.0 (names, offsets, masks and shifts)
struct.doc: Consecutive negative-acknowledge counter for processor B, named PI_NACK_CNT_B in the header. The IRIX register table confirms the access.

struct.name: PI_NACK_CMP
struct.from: public Linux SN0 Hub processor-interface header, Linux v4.0 (names, offsets, masks and shifts)
struct.doc: Negative-acknowledge compare, named PI_NACK_CMP in the header. The header gives a maximum of 0x0fffff for the count, so the compare is twenty bits wide. The IRIX register table confirms the access.
